cleansingStrength.rationale: Moderate: SLES is the primary cleanser, but it is buffered by amphoteric betaines and a visibly conditioning/refatting chassis; helper emulsifiers are not counted as separate cleansing routes.
cleansingStrength.counterSignal: SLES at position 2 and sodium chloride at position 4 keep the formula from a low-cleansing call.

conditioningLevel.rationale: High: early dimethicone, early cationic guar, late amodimethicone and early glycol distearate create several complementary rinse-off slip and manageability routes.
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: The product is still a rinse-off SLES shampoo, and the dm conflict shifts amodimethicone later rather than strengthening the care call.

weightPotential.rationale: Moderate: silicone plus cationic polymer deposition makes noticeable residue plausible, while SLES/betaine cleansing and late amodimethicone keep the band below high.

formulaFacts.observation: reset capacity from primary anionic cleanser

weightPotential.counterSignal: The same formula has meaningful cleansing reset and no heavy oil/butter stack; the dm conflict moves amodimethicone only from late to later.

unresolvedFacts: Exact silicone/polymer concentrations are not knowable from INCI order alone.
Same-GTIN dm formula changes color/fragrance exposure and shifts amodimethicone from late position 23 to late position 25 without changing the weight-bearing routes.
weightAssessment.whyThisBand: One early nonvolatile silicone route plus cationic guar can plausibly reduce movement over repeated use.
weightAssessment.whyNotNeighborBand: Not high because SLES/betaine cleansing provides real reset and the additional amodimethicone route is late in both preserved formulas.

focusPrimary.rationale: General: the dominant exact-product claim is hydration/moisture, which is compatible with sodium hyaluronate and conditioning routes but is not a v1.4 focus enum.

formulaFacts.observation: smoothing route compatible with cosmetic hydration positioning

focusPrimary.counterSignal: There is a shine phrase, but hydration is the range/name-dominant positioning.

focusSecondary.rationale: Shine is a bounded secondary: the manufacturer separately promises shiny, lively hair, and the formula has silicone smoothing plus acid/pH clues independent from the moisture claim.
focusSecondary.counterSignal: Shine is not the product-name dominant promise and should not replace the primary general mapping for hydration.

usageRole.rationale: Regular: the packet provides ordinary rinse-out directions and no explicit daily, treatment, alternating, clarifying or reset trigger.
usageRole.counterSignal: SLES makes cleansing meaningful, but v1.4 says strong cleansing alone would still not create an alternating role.

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: Not targeted: the product mentions scalp hydration but is not positioned for sensitive, itchy or uncomfortable scalp, and fragrance exposure plus SLES prevent treating it as a comfort-targeted formula.
scalpComfortTarget.counterSignal: The manufacturer says the formula moisturizes scalp and lengths, so the absence of a sensitive-scalp claim is the limiting factor rather than absent scalp wording.

dandruffSupport.rationale: Not supported: the complete canonical formula contains neither Piroctone Olamine nor Climbazole; salicylic acid alone is explicitly not enough under v1.4.
